claim: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's minimum natural alcohol, the highest of any French appellation, is:
because: The keyed 12.5% is correct (the CdP cahier des charges sets a minimum natural alcohol of 12.5%). But it is not the highest minimum in France. The Sauternes cahier des charges sets a minimum natural alcohol of 15%, with grapes of at least 221 g/l sugar. Even among southern Rhône dry reds, the Gigondas cahier also requires 12.5%, so Châteauneuf does not stand alone at that figure either. A candidate who learns 'highest in France' will get any comparison question wrong.
